reading.body:
Santa Clara II represents one-fifth of California's published data center power capacity at 75 MW, placing it in a thin tier of operator transparency across the state's 103 mapped facilities.

The facility is a three-building campus totaling 541,000 square feet on nine acres in Silicon Valley, less than two miles from Vantage's Santa Clara I facility. At typical AI training density, the 75 MW capacity could support roughly 1,875 racks, though the operator does not publish how the power is distributed across the three buildings or allocated by workload. Power comes from three on-site 50 MW transformers served by Silicon Valley Power. Combined with Santa Clara I, Vantage controls 152 MW of announced capacity in the region, making it a material concentration of grid-dependent infrastructure in a constrained power market.

Only 11 of California's 103 mapped data center facilities publish capacity figures. Santa Clara II's inclusion in this sparse group makes it visible as infrastructure, but also masks the state's total deployed compute. Without building-level breakdowns or utilization data, the 75 MW figure does not reveal whether the full capacity is deployed, available, or limited by local power supply constraints. The absence of certifications or tenant deployments in public records prevents assessment of what workloads run here or how they compete for Silicon Valley Power's constrained supply.
